---
title: "Glossary"
---

Terms used in the course, in alphabetical order. Each entry names the modules that use it.
Clinical terms are defined in plain words for engineers; they are not clinical guidance.

Ablation
: Destroying a small area of heart tissue on purpose, for example by radiofrequency heating, to stop an arrhythmia. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Action potential
: The rise and fall of the transmembrane voltage when a heart cell is excited. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Activation wavefront
: The moving boundary between excited and resting tissue. Also called the front. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

AI agent
: A program in which a model, usually a large language model, chooses step by step which tool to call, reads the result and continues until a goal is met or a step limit is reached. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Arrhythmia
: An abnormal heart rhythm. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Atrial fibrillation (AF)
: A fast, irregular rhythm of the upper chambers, without organized atrial activity. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Atrium (plural atria)
: One of the two upper chambers of the heart. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Attention
: In a neural network, a weighted average of value vectors whose weights come from how well a query matches each key, normalized by a softmax. The building block of the transformer. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Audit log
: An append-only record of every step an agent took: the tool, its arguments, the policy decision and the result, so a person can check the run afterwards. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Average precision (PR AUC)
: The area under the precision–recall curve, averaged over thresholds. Unlike the ROC AUC it falls when positives are rare. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Average symmetric surface distance (ASSD)
: The mean distance between two surfaces, measured from each to the other; a typical-error measure for segmentations. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Bayesian optimization
: Choosing where to measure next by modelling an unknown function with a probabilistic surrogate, such as a Gaussian process, and maximizing an acquisition function. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Bipolar electrogram
: The difference between the signals of two nearby electrodes. It acts like a spatial derivative: it keeps local detail and rejects distant activity, but depends on the bipole's orientation to the wavefront. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Clique
: A small group of electrodes, such as a triangle or a square, whose bipoles are combined to estimate the local electric field. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Collocation point
: A point where a governing equation is checked during fitting; it needs no measurement. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Concordance index (C index)
: For a risk score, the share of comparable patient pairs in which the patient with the earlier event had the higher score; 0.5 is chance. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Conduction velocity
: The speed at which the activation wavefront travels through tissue, in m/s (1 m/s = 1 mm/ms). [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd), [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Contrastive learning
: Self-supervised learning that pulls the embeddings of matched pairs, such as two recordings of one patient, together and pushes unmatched pairs apart. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Cross-entropy
: The loss most classifiers minimize: minus the log of the probability given to the true class. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Data augmentation
: Training on altered copies of the data (for example, flipped or noisier signals) so a model ignores the alteration. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Dataset shift
: Any difference between the data a model was trained on and the data where it is used: in class mix (prior shift), in the recordings (covariate shift) or in what labels mean. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Decapolar catheter
: A catheter with ten electrodes along its shaft. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd), [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Dice coefficient
: Overlap of a predicted and a true region: twice the shared area over the sum of the two areas, from 0 (no overlap) to 1 (identical). [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd), [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Eikonal equation
: The equation v |grad T| = 1 linking an activation-time map T to the local conduction speed v. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Electrogram
: The voltage an electrode records from currents crossing cell membranes nearby. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Embedding
: A vector that represents an input, such as a beat or a sentence, so that similar inputs get nearby vectors. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Endocardium
: The inner surface of the heart wall. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Ensemble
: A set of models trained with different random choices; their spread is used as an uncertainty estimate. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Expected improvement
: An acquisition function: the average amount by which a new measurement is expected to beat the best value so far. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

External validation
: Testing a frozen model on data from another place or time that played no part in training or tuning. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Far-field signal
: Activity that an electrode picks up from tissue that is not directly under it. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Federated learning
: Training one model across sites that keep their data; only model updates are shared. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Fibrosis
: Replacement of heart muscle by connective tissue. In the atria it can be estimated on late-gadolinium MRI. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Focal loss
: A cross-entropy that down-weights examples the model already gets right, so training attends to rare and hard ones. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Focal source
: A small region from which activation spreads outward. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Foundation model
: A large model pretrained on broad, mostly unlabeled data and then adapted to many downstream tasks. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Gaussian mixture model
: A probability model that describes data as a weighted sum of normal distributions; fitted with the EM algorithm to find clusters without labels. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Gaussian process
: A probability model over functions; given measurements, it gives a mean estimate and an uncertainty at every other point. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Geodesic distance
: The length of the shortest path between two points that stays on a surface. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Graph convolution
: A network layer that mixes each point's features with those of its neighbours on a graph, such as the vertices of a mapping mesh. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Guardrail
: A rule enforced outside the model that limits what an agent may do, such as a tool allowlist, a schema check or a human approval step. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Hallucination
: Output of a language model that reads as fluent and confident but is false or unsupported, such as an invented number or reference. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Hausdorff distance
: The largest distance from any point of one surface to the other surface, in either direction; one stray island sets it. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Human approval step
: A point in an agent's run where a person must accept or decline an action, such as any write, before it is carried out. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Implantable loop recorder (ILR)
: A small device placed under the skin that records the ECG for years and sends alerts when its detector fires. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE)
: Ultrasound imaging from a catheter inside the heart, used during procedures to see anatomy and build shells. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Intrinsic deflection
: The steepest downstroke of a unipolar electrogram, used to mark local activation. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Jaccard index
: Overlap of two regions as intersection over union; Dice = 2J/(1 + J). [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Large language model (LLM)
: A transformer trained on very large amounts of text to predict the next token; it can follow instructions and answer questions in text. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)
: MRI taken some minutes after a gadolinium contrast injection, when scar and fibrosis appear bright. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Leave-one-patient-out
: A test scheme that trains on all patients but one and tests on that one, in turn, so no patient is in both sets. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Levenberg–Marquardt method
: An iterative method for nonlinear least squares that blends Gauss–Newton steps with damped gradient steps. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Linear probe
: A linear classifier trained on the frozen features of a pretrained model, used to measure how much those features already encode. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Local activation time
: The moment the activation wavefront reaches a given site. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Low-voltage area
: A region whose bipolar voltage falls below a chosen cut-off. It is often read as scar, but the voltage also depends on the catheter and the wavefront. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Myocardial infarction
: Death of an area of heart muscle caused by loss of its blood supply. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Normalized surface Dice (NSD)
: The share of two surfaces lying within a chosen tolerance of each other. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Omnipolar electrogram
: A signal built from a clique by estimating the local electric field and reading it along the direction of propagation, which removes most orientation dependence. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Outflow tract
: The part of a ventricle leading to its great artery (pulmonary artery on the right, aorta on the left); a common origin of idiopathic premature ventricular beats. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Pace mapping
: Pacing from a catheter at candidate sites and comparing the paced 12-lead ECG with the ECG of the arrhythmia, to find where the arrhythmia starts. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Pacing
: Stimulating the heart electrically from an electrode at a chosen site. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Photoplethysmography (PPG)
: Measuring blood-volume changes in tissue with light; the basis of pulse sensing in watches and trackers. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Physics-informed neural network (PINN)
: A neural network trained on a loss that adds the residual of a governing equation to the data misfit. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Positive predictive value (PPV)
: The share of positive results (alerts, flags) that are truly positive; it depends on prevalence. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd), [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Premature beat
: A beat that comes earlier than expected, usually followed by a longer interval; a common cause of false AF alerts. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Premature ventricular contraction (PVC)
: An extra beat that starts in a ventricle earlier than the next normal beat. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Prompt injection
: Text inside a document or tool output that tries to make a language model follow new instructions, such as a hidden request to delete files. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI)
: Ablation that encircles the pulmonary veins so that their electrical activity cannot reach the left atrium. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd), [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Radial basis function
: A function of the distance to a centre, such as a Gaussian; sums of them represent smooth maps. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Receptive field
: The stretch of input that one output of a network depends on. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Remote monitoring
: Sending data from an implanted or wearable device to a clinic, where alerts are reviewed. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
: Answering with a language model after giving it passages retrieved from a chosen document collection, so that the answer can rest on, and cite, those passages. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

RR interval
: The time between two successive R peaks of the ECG, one ventricular beat to the next. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Scar
: Fibrous tissue that has replaced heart muscle. It conducts poorly or not at all. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Segmentation
: Labelling which voxels of an image belong to a structure, such as the left atrium. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Self-supervised learning
: Learning representations from unlabeled data with a training task built from the data themselves, such as matching two views of one recording. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Sinus rhythm
: The normal heartbeat, started by the heart's own pacemaker. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Softmax
: The function that turns a vector of scores into probabilities that are positive and sum to one. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Spatial frequency
: How quickly a pattern varies in space, in rad/mm. Fine detail has high spatial frequency. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Surrogate model
: A fast approximation of a slow model, fitted to runs of it and valid only in the range it was trained on. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

TF-IDF
: Term frequency times inverse document frequency: a word weight that grows with how often the word appears in a document and with how rare it is across the collection. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Token
: A unit of text, often a word or part of a word, that a language model reads and writes. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Tool schema
: The declared arguments of an agent's tool, with their types, units and allowed ranges, checked before the tool runs. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Transformer
: A neural-network architecture built from attention layers; the basis of most large language models and of many ECG foundation models. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Transmembrane voltage
: The voltage across a cell membrane, inside minus outside. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Unipolar electrogram
: The signal of one electrode measured against a distant reference electrode. It sees local and far-field activity. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Ventricle
: One of the two lower chambers of the heart. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Ventricular tachycardia
: A fast rhythm that starts in the ventricles. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd), [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Volume conductor
: The conducting medium (tissue and blood) through which currents spread from their sources to the electrodes. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)
